Package io.webagent4j.recording.replay

Class ReplayValidator

java.lang.Object
io.webagent4j.recording.replay.ReplayValidator
public final class ReplayValidator extends Object
Validates that a WorkflowRecordingV2 is eligible for Deterministic Replay against a live Workflow, before any replay of its recorded trace begins.

recording is treated as fully untrusted input; workflow is treated as trusted, live structure. validate(io.webagent4j.recording.WorkflowRecordingV2, io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow) invokes nothing on workflow beyond WorkflowPlanner.plan(Workflow) - it never evaluates a condition, never invokes an IWorkflowActionFactory, and never performs any side effect. It is pure and stateless: the same two arguments always produce the same result, and calling it never mutates either argument.

Replay eligibility rests on two independent guarantees, not one: (1) recording.nodes() is itself a structurally authorized path through recording.plan() - the same step IDs, types, and declared outputs at the same positions, and every recorded branch selection corresponding exclusively to that plan node's matching branch - and (2) recording.plan() matches the live workflow's current structure. The first is a precondition this class relies on rather than re-derives: WorkflowRecordingV2's own compact constructor (see RecordingV2PlanTreeValidator) already guarantees it for every possible construction path, so no WorkflowRecordingV2 instance can exist whose tree is inconsistent with its own plan. validate(io.webagent4j.recording.WorkflowRecordingV2, io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow) only checks the second: recording.plan() (captured once, at record time) compared for exact equality against WorkflowPlanner.plan(workflow) (recomputed fresh, from workflow's current definition). WorkflowPlanner.plan(io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow) is deterministic and reads only a workflow's static step structure, so this equality check is exactly "does workflow's current step structure - types, guards, declared outputs, and conditional branch shapes - still match what was recorded," independent of whatever runtime input values a caller might supply. A structural change to the workflow definition since capture (a step added, removed, retyped, or reordered) always fails this check. Matching the recorded plan alone was never sufficient on its own - a plan match says nothing about whether the recorded tree paired with it is genuine - which is exactly why guarantee (1) exists as a separate, unconditionally-enforced precondition rather than being folded into this equality check.

Why only COMPLETED is supported: replaying a FAILED recording's trace is out of scope for this initial structural/decision-replay implementation - see ReplayFailureType.UNSUPPORTED_STATUS. This is a deliberate, documented scope decision, not an oversight: a future revision may define what replaying a failure means, but this one does not guess at it.

This validator does not itself replay anything and returns no context for doing so - a separate replay-execution step consumes an already-validated recording/workflow pair to reconstruct the recorded decision trace.
